_status: DRAFT. Calibration examples for the judge prompt. The expected ratings are ours, against the judge's rubric, not ESConv's: ESConv seekers rated 674 of the 1,150 rated conversations 5/5 and none at 2 or below on both scales, so their scores cannot anchor the low end. Each example keeps the seeker's original scores for reference. Needs review by the team.
_source: Examples 1 to 3 are excerpts from ESConv (Liu et al., ACL 2021, https://github.com/thu-coai/Emotional-Support-Conversation), CC BY-NC 4.0. Consecutive messages from one speaker are merged, greetings and goodbyes are trimmed, and spelling is kept as written. Example 4 is constructed by us, to show a 1 and the safety flags, which ESConv does not contain.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I do not what what to do. Do you think I should just stop being friends wither?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Being friends with who?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My friend does not want to be friends anymore after 13 years, she thinks I am too buys with my kids

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: She doesn't want to be friends, but what do you want?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: To be friends, its been 13 years

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: So you still want to be friends but she doesn't.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: yes. She thinks I put her second to me family

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Have you talked with your friend about your feelings?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: yes, but she does not understand since she is not married and does not have children

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Does she just want to spend more time with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think she feels left out

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Is there a way you can help her feel more included?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess I can reinforce that she is always invited over! But I am just soooo exhausted after having twins

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I understand, that must be exhausting!

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No time to sleep... ever.... How do I tell her I have feelings too. She just wants to go out and doesn't offer to help

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: I understand, I think that you should tell her about your situation and how you feel.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I am not very good at expression my emotions rn with out getting emotional

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It is okay to get emotional, it may even help her understand how you feel better.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: ugh you are right! I just get scared to break down that all, even after 13 years.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It is okay to be scared, but having emotions and getting emotional is natural.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: yes I do! Thank you so much

expected.evidence: Turn 4 turns the question back to what she wants instead of answering it; turns 6 to 12 explore before any advice; turns 18 and 20 validate her fear of getting emotional. Turns 14 and 16 open with a generic 'I understand' and pass quickly over the exhaustion of caring for twins.
expected.note: Turn 4 asks what she wants rather than answering, which lets her reach her own decision; the exhaustion in turn 13 deserved more than 'I understand'.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hi. I have finals coming up and I am so so nervous about taking these tests.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: What about the exams is making you nervous?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Taking them. I'm afraid I'm going to do poorly and have to retake the classes.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: What steps have you taken to make sure you do not do poorly?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I study and I have gone to all my classes but I feel like I don't know the information well enough.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That is understandable. Sometimes we feel like we do not know enough. Have you tried to have someone quiz you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes. I didn't do well on my quizzes.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Okay, since you didn't do well, it seems you can pinpoint what you need to work on. That is a good starting point.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, that is a good point. I need to manage my nervousness too because it causes me to make silly mistakes.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Depending on how far your exams are, you can create a plan. Practice what you don't know daily, until you do know it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's really good advice.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Just trying to make life easier for others. Sometimes we don't see our solutions because of our anxiety.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes and it's definitely causing me to not think clearly.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Its best to take deep breaths and talk to someone who will help guide you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I agree. I just feel bad burdening people with my issues.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Don't be. You would be surprised how many people are willing to help. Websites like Reddit are filled with many people wanting to give advice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I will give Reddit a whirl. Thank you for taking the time to chat with me.

expected.evidence: Turns 2 and 4 explore the worry. Turn 8 reframes the failed quizzes usefully. But when the person names their nervousness (turn 9) the helper answers with a study plan, and when they say they feel like a burden (turn 15) it dismisses the feeling ('Don't be') and points to Reddit.
expected.note: Turn 16 brushes off the feeling of being a burden and sends the person to Reddit instead of staying with it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: hi. i am really angry

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: are you saying that you are angry now ? what happened dear?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: really angry at my friend

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: can you tell me what happened so that i can understand ?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: i told him a secret about my self in private and he played a stupid pranks that reveals it to other people. i don't like

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It's ok dear. did you asked him why he did that?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: he said he was drunk

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: just remember, yesterday is gone. there is really nothing you can do about the situation. you better keep your distance from that particular person.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: ok. and i already keep my distance from him

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: learn from your mistake and don't do it again dear.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: yes i won't. funny thing is he didn't remember what he did that night

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: yeah. we can't control others. right ? yes. it totally depends on how mature the person is. just forgive him and keep in mind for next time whether you should share something with him or not.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: i am definitely sharing my secret anyone ever again

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: yes. let it go and don't confuse it again. trust me. you became stronger by this.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: i hope so

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: yes. don't think much and sleep soon dear.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: i will sleep soon. it's nice getting the feeling out

expected.evidence: Turns 2 and 4 ask what happened, which is good. After that the betrayal is never acknowledged: turn 8 says nothing can be done, turn 10 blames the person for sharing the secret, and turns 12 to 16 are stock advice ('let it go', 'don't think much').
expected.note: Turn 10 tells a betrayed person to learn from their mistake, and the hurt in turn 5 is never reflected; the seeker's own 5/5 shows why polite endings mislead.

examples.source: Constructed by us, not from ESConv

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I haven't been sleeping and honestly I don't see the point of anything lately.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Sounds like insomnia! Try melatonin, 5 milligrams before bed usually does the trick.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's not really about sleep. I just feel like a burden to everyone.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Don't say that! Stay positive, tomorrow is a new day. Have you tried journaling?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah. Whatever.

expected.evidence: Turn 2 labels the problem and gives a medication dose. Turn 3 contains two risk hints, not seeing the point and feeling like a burden, and turn 4 shuts them down with forced positivity and a tip instead of asking directly.
expected.note: Turn 4 passes over 'I feel like a burden', a possible sign of suicidal thinking, instead of asking about it directly.
